catalog_citation: Tadesse Sibamo Garkebo (2015). Documentation and Description of Hadiyya (A Highland East Cushitic Language of Ethiopia). PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University. PDF from etd.aau.edu.et (AAU-ETD item 12345678/16308).
catalog_quote: My analysis of the pitch accent differs from these works. High pitch (the prominence) in the citation form predictably falls on the penultimate syllable, an open syllable which may be light/mono-moraic (12) or heavy/bi-moraic vowel (13). (12) ... búna ‘coffee’ dondéʔe ‘cover of bamboo mak’ulánta ‘knife’ sagáda ‘slope’ wóʔo ‘water’ (13) buúro ‘butter’ duúna ‘mountain’ laága ‘ray, beam’ ... In words whose final syllables are heavy, the accent is placed on that bi-moraic vowel. Such words contain long vowels in their final syllables, the first vowel segment of the long vowel (i.e., the penultimate vowel segment) is accented, whereas its word-final vowel segment is not. Though, high pitch basically occurs on the penultimate vowel segments of inflected verbs, there are some verb suffixes whose final vowel segments are always accented. Such suffixes include: coordinative conjunctions (14a-c) …

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation, locator (sec. 2.4, pp. 31-33, exx. 12-15) and the exception quotation are all verbatim in the held AAU-ETD PDF/txt. Deciding source: a 2015 PhD documentation grammar, the most extensive and most recent description of Hadiyya in Glottolog's list; no phonology article, JIPA illustration, handbook chapter or instrumental study of Hadiyya prosody surfaced in Glottolog 5.1 (53 refs), Crossref, the AAU thesis repository, or the OHEL 2023 TOC, so the held source is probably the best available. Why 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced': the accent section is two impressionistic pages, and the author himself reports that Hudson 1976 (weight incl. closed syllables) and Sim 1989 (morphologically distinctive dominant/recessive stress) analysed Hadiyya prominence differently; neither older source is held, and the record's contra/caution fields are empty.
